## 5 · Clean the coarse mesh
Direct3D-V3 keeps what the coarse mesh gives it, so clean it first.

**Switch** (bottom): `true` = **WTiVo** watertight (768 / 6M points, ~35 s, far fewer loose parts after refine). `false` = **Remesh ×2** (faster, more floaters).

nodes.title: Note
widgets_values:
## 6 · Direct3D-V3, maximum detail
The recipe that gave the most detail in the tests: the **clay image** from the group below as the reference, **16 steps**, `guidance_mode` **fdg** with `fdg_high_scale` **9**, **single stage** at 1536, and the **raw** coarse mesh (the cleanup group is not connected here).

About 100 s of sampling on an RTX 5080 for a small character; same VRAM as the default.

Cleaner mesh, slightly less fine detail: connect the cleanup **Switch** output to `coarse_mesh`.

Result: `output/Direct3D-V3/refined_max_detail_<id>.glb`.

Nodes by Mstafa-awad, model by DreamTechAI (MIT).

widgets_values_named.text:
## 6 · Direct3D-V3
Refines the mesh against your image at 1536.

**Tuned settings:** 16 steps + `accel_mode: lossless` → ~3 min, VRAM peak ~11 GiB. Versus 8 steps/`fast`: 4.6× fewer loose parts, 3.7× fewer holes. Faster but rougher: 8 steps + `fast` (~2 min).

`max_tokens` 150k is not limiting (this character uses ~61k at 1536).

Result: `output/Direct3D-V3/refined_1536_<id>.glb` (~7M faces).

Nodes by Mstafa-awad, model by DreamTechAI (MIT).

Every interlocking piece has strong independent relief. A deeply recessed narrow channel with a distinctly near-black floor separates adjacent parts. Sharply defined raised lips catch a bright highlight. Retain the actual width and path of each seam. Resolve tiny real features as crisp secondary relief. Keep the base of every fine contact dark, the sloping inner wall legible and the small crest clean. Separate scales, directional facial folds, engraved motifs and part edges wherever they appear. Follow the input structure closely. Preserve interruptions, variations and smooth spaces in the original. Hard raking key, strong local cavity occlusion, a little reflected light on the shaded sidewalls, strikingly readable fine detail. Matte monochrome graphite-gray clay, all paint and printed patterns removed. Keep each valley narrow and preserve its actual interruption points and corner radii. Preserve the tiniest intentionally shaped ridges, scales and recessed joins. Flat panel interiors and all unbroken curved surfaces have perfectly clean continuous shading. Grain-free digital studio render.

nodes.title: Clay prompt + your image
Note
widgets_values:
## Clay reference image
Qwen Image 2.1 turns your image into a grey clay render (prompt by the Direct3D-V3 authors). Direct3D-V3 reads shapes better from it than from a colour image. About 3.5 minutes; TRELLIS.2 and UltraTex still use your original image.

Needs the Qwen Image 2.1 models (`qwen_image_2.1_int8_convrot`, `qwen3vl_8b_int8_convrot`, `qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16`). Check the clay image in the preview: it must show the same pose and view as your image.

nodes.title: Note
widgets_values:
## 7 to 9 · Texture with UltraTex (MostAadTech's UTX nodes)
GGUF models, 10 views at 1024, albedo, baked at 2048. More quality on bigger cards: `view_resolution` 2048 in **Generate texture views** and `texture_size` 4096 in **Bake texture**.

No texture wanted? Select groups 7 to 9 and bypass them.

Models: `flux-2-klein-base-9b-Q4_0.gguf`, `Qwen3-8B-Q6_K.gguf`, `flux2-vae`, `ultratex_flux2` LoRA, `ultratex_flux2_decoder`. FLUX.2 klein base 9B is under the FLUX Non-Commercial License.
